issues.body: `read_health_window` deliberately publishes `None` on an unreadable ledger, which becomes `worker_no_change_rate_1h: null`. `_worker_no_change_pred` returns false for that null, and `compute_recoveries` interprets `not any(pred(row) ...)` as confirmed clearance. Therefore, after `recover_snapshots` consecutive ledger-read failures, a collected target is eligible to auto-close its existing `worker-no-change` alert even though there is no evidence the condition cleared. The collection-token guard does not help because the target itself was collected successfully; only this auxiliary signal is absent. The current tests assert that null does not fire, but never assert that null does not recover, so this fail-open path remains uncovered.
issues.fix_hint: Make recovery tri-state for this class: distinguish measurable-and-clear from unavailable. Require every recovery-window row to contain a numeric no-change rate (and the sample semantics needed by the predicate) before adding `WORKER_NO_CHANGE` to recoveries. Add a non-vacuous test starting from an existing alert/recovery candidate and show that two null-rate snapshots do not produce the `(target, WORKER_NO_CHANGE)` recovery key, while two measured healthy snapshots still do.
issues.title: Unreadable no-change telemetry can auto-close a live alert

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new no-change alert fires fail-closed on missing telemetry, but its recovery path does not: two unreadable-ledger snapshots are treated as two clear snapshots and can auto-close an existing alert. That contradicts the stated null-as-no-evidence contract and the reconciler's own requirement for confirmed recovery. Because round 3 had no findings and this is a new major finding, progress is regressing.
